cards.noteEnglish: The source says the word is used for men and women. The Reader uses la barista for the woman in this scene.
Everyday French expresses feeling sleepy with avoir sommeil; this is a contextual gloss for the noun sleepiness.

cards.supportEnglish: Good morning, how are you this morning?
cards.noteEnglish: Polite vous form. Source also gives an informal Spanish variant; a French informal equivalent needs qualified review.

cards.supportEnglish: It is very cold today, isn't it?
cards.targetFrench: Il fait très froid aujourd'hui, n'est-ce pas ?

cards.supportEnglish: I am still a little sleepy.
cards.sourceSpanish: Todavía tengo un poco de sueño.

cards.supportEnglish: I am going to visit downtown if it does not rain.
cards.sourceSpanish: Voy a visitar el centro si no llueve.
cards.targetFrench: Je vais visiter le centre-ville s'il ne pleut pas.

cards.supportEnglish: Sorry, can you repeat that more slowly, please?
cards.sourceSpanish: Perdón, ¿puede repetir más despacio, por favor?
cards.targetFrench: Pardon, pouvez-vous répéter plus lentement, s'il vous plaît ?

cards.supportEnglish: You too, have a good day!

reader.supportEnglish: It is early and I am in a small café, waiting for my coffee with milk at the counter.
reader.sourceSpanish: Es temprano y estoy en una cafetería pequeña, esperando mi café con leche en el mostrador.
reader.targetFrench: Il est tôt et je suis dans un petit café, où j'attends mon café au lait au comptoir.

reader.supportEnglish: The barista smiles at me and says: Good morning, how are you this morning?
reader.sourceSpanish: La barista me sonríe y dice: Buenos días, ¿cómo amaneció?
reader.targetFrench: La barista me sourit et dit : « Bonjour, comment allez-vous ce matin ? »

reader.supportEnglish: I answer: Very well, thanks, but I am still a little sleepy.
reader.sourceSpanish: Yo respondo: Muy bien, gracias, pero todavía tengo un poco de sueño.
reader.targetFrench: Je réponds : « Très bien, merci, mais j'ai encore un peu sommeil. »

reader.supportEnglish: She comments that it is cold today because it rained last night, and I tell her the weather is very different in my country.
reader.sourceSpanish: Ella comenta que hoy hace frío porque anoche llovió, y yo le digo que el clima está muy distinto en mi país.
reader.targetFrench: Elle fait remarquer qu'il fait froid aujourd'hui parce qu'il a plu hier soir, et je lui dis que le temps est très différent dans mon pays.

reader.supportEnglish: A man near me asks: What plans do you have for today?
reader.sourceSpanish: Un señor cerca de mí pregunta: ¿Qué planes tiene para hoy?
reader.targetFrench: Un monsieur près de moi demande : « Quels projets avez-vous pour aujourd'hui ? »

reader.supportEnglish: I explain that I am going to visit downtown if it does not rain again.
reader.sourceSpanish: Le explico que voy a visitar el centro si no llueve otra vez.
reader.targetFrench: Je lui explique que je vais visiter le centre-ville s'il ne pleut pas de nouveau.

reader.supportEnglish: He recommends that I bring a coat, because according to the forecast the afternoon is going to be cool.
reader.sourceSpanish: Él me recomienda llevar un abrigo, porque según el pronóstico la tarde va a estar fresca.
reader.targetFrench: Il me recommande de prendre un manteau, car, selon les prévisions, l'après-midi sera frais.

reader.supportEnglish: When my order is ready, the barista tells me: Have a great day!
reader.sourceSpanish: Cuando mi pedido está listo, la barista me dice: ¡Que le vaya muy bien!
reader.targetFrench: Quand ma commande est prête, la barista me dit : « Passez une excellente journée ! »

reader.supportEnglish: I answer with a smile: You too, have a good day!
reader.sourceSpanish: Le contesto con una sonrisa: ¡Igualmente, que tenga un buen día!
reader.targetFrench: Je lui réponds avec un sourire : « Vous aussi, bonne journée ! »

forms.frenchExample: Aujourd'hui, il fait froid au café.
forms.supportEnglish: Today it is cold at the café.
forms.explanationEnglish: Faire is irregular (je fais, tu fais, il fait, nous faisons, ils font). For weather, French uses impersonal il fait plus an adjective: il fait froid, il fait chaud, like Spanish hace frío, hace calor.

forms.supportEnglish: I wait for my coffee at the counter.
forms.explanationEnglish: Attendre takes a direct object with no preposition: attendre mon café. Spanish esperar here maps to French attendre, not espérer (which means to hope).

forms.frenchExample: Il me recommande de prendre un manteau.
forms.supportEnglish: He recommends that I bring a coat.
forms.explanationEnglish: French recommander is a regular -er verb with no stem change. The Spanish e-to-ie stem change does not carry over. Use de plus an infinitive for the advice: recommander de prendre.

forms.frenchExample: Aujourd'hui, je visite le centre-ville avec mon ami.
forms.supportEnglish: Today I visit downtown with my friend.
forms.explanationEnglish: Visiter is a regular -er verb and takes a direct object with no preposition: visiter le centre-ville. The source example is in the present tense, so the same present form is used here.

forms.frenchExample: Un monsieur me demande quels sont mes projets.
forms.supportEnglish: A man asks me about my plans.
forms.explanationEnglish: Demander means to ask. It takes à plus the person (me = à moi) and the thing asked: demander quelque chose à quelqu'un. Here the thing asked is the clause quels sont mes projets.

objectivesEnglish: Greet the barista and answer how you are this morning, saying you are still a little sleepy.
React to the barista's remark that it is cold today because it rained last night, and say the weather is very different in your country.
When the customer near you (un monsieur) asks about your plans for today, explain to him that you are going to visit downtown if it does not rain again.
Respond to the customer's recommendation to bring a coat because, according to the forecast, the afternoon is going to be cool.
When your order is ready and the barista wishes you well, close the exchange by replying "You too, have a good day!"

notes: Private editorial draft only; not qualified approval, not released, and no learner, audio, progress, or review gate is open. All gates remain false.
Reader core:11:line:4: Spanish anoche and English last night are rendered as hier soir; cette nuit is the alternative if the rain is understood as overnight. Reviewer choice; not treated as an error.
Spanish recomendar (one m) corresponds to French recommander (two m's). The Spanish infinitive is copied exactly as given in the source.

Forms explanations: the faire conjugation and weather pattern, and the demander quelque chose à quelqu'un construction, are stated from general French knowledge alongside the source notes and should be checked by a reviewer. The earlier unsourced prescription against questionner has been removed, and the faire explanation no longer links irregularity to the weather expression.

audioPending is true on Hear and Say because both depend on audio that does not exist: no audio was generated, assumed or approved. Hear stays scriptOnly. audioPending false on See, Recall, Type and Write means the mode needs no audio; it does not mean audio is ready.

IDs are now 1-based (core:11:word:1..17, core:11:line:1..9) with the source sequence preserved, and every mode sourceCardId was shifted to match. Modes are differentiated by task: See is recognition, Recall is production from a situation, Type is exact transcription of the shown target, and Write is composition with every element of the target cued.

Speaking: a third role, customer (the source's un señor), was added. The plans question and the coat recommendation are attributed to the customer, and the remark about cold and last night's rain to the barista, as in source lines 4, 5 and 7. Objectives are drawn from source lines only.

English cool in the source is rendered as frais; no weather facts beyond the source were added. Reader core:11:line:6 restores the indirect object of Le explico (Je lui explique). The forms examples now read Aujourd'hui, il fait froid au café. and Un monsieur me demande quels sont mes projets. No additional approvals or release state is implied.

Source-grounded self-check after Fable changed the card-only noun gloss for sleepiness from le sommeil (sleep) to l'envie de dormir (the feeling of wanting to sleep) and carried the source's barista gender note onto the card. Qualified French/dictionary review should choose the final headword.
